stories.title: Meta's Muse lands on iPad a month after its mobile debut as the chart-topping agent's troubles pile up

Meta's Muse, a personal AI agent built on its Muse Spark model platform, is topping app store charts and growing faster than ChatGPT did at launch, and Meta keeps widening its reach even as privacy, security, platform, originality, and labor trouble accumulate.

- New: Muse is now available on iPad, just a month after its mobile debut, as Meta rapidly expands the assistant's reach and integrations
- Meta disputes a journalist's account that Muse read his private Messages while the required Mac permission was off, saying the agent cannot access Messages without explicit permission
- Gizmodo reports Meta tested routing some Muse tasks through a "human concierge" of contractors who make the agent's phone calls, one of whom reportedly made racist remarks
- Meta says Muse was built from scratch but admits it was "heavily inspired" by OpenClaw, down to some workspace filenames and content
- Ars Technica reports a serious 0-day in the highly privileged agent that could have let attackers do "whatever" they wanted on a victim's Mac; Meta says it has issued a fix
- Amazon has blocked the Muse agent from shopping on Amazon.com, citing privacy and security concerns

- Clayton, the director of national intelligence, will lead the task force, per Gizmodo; Trump had earlier promised to fill the post when announcing an "AI Force"

- The rebrand is backed by an executive order, "Inaugurating the Era of Super Intelligence," signed September 29, directing federal agencies to say "Super Intelligence" instead of AI

- Commentators at Mashable and Gizmodo note the new label changes nothing about the technology's underlying problems
